title: Deref coercion
summary: &String converts to &str automatically (and &Vec<T> to &[T]) at call sites.
lecture: When a function wants &str and you pass &String, the compiler inserts the conversion for you — this is deref coercion, driven by String implementing Deref<Target = str>. The same applies to &Vec<T> coercing to &[T], and &Box<T> to &T.

The practical consequence flows one way: a parameter typed &str accepts &String, string literals, and sub-slices alike, while a parameter typed &String accepts only &String. That is why &str is strictly more useful in a signature and why Clippy's ptr_arg lint flags &String and &Vec<T> parameters.
Coercion happens silently at call sites, so you mostly notice it by its absence — when a signature demands the owning type and suddenly nothing fits.

example.caption: One &str parameter serves owned strings and literals alike.
